title: After eating
hook: praise to Allah who fed me this without power from me (Abu Dawud; Tirmidhi)
tomorrow: worry and grief: are they the same thing?

segments.voice: Yesterday, entering the mosque: Your mercy going in, Your bounty going out. Mercy in, bounty out. Today, the end of a meal.
screen: `MERCY IN, BOUNTY OUT.` → `THE END OF A MEAL.`

segments.voice: A plate set in front of you by someone else's hands. Maybe a friend's mother who wouldn't let you help, or pay, or even carry your dish to the sink. Maybe a cafeteria tray, cooked by people you'll never see. Either way the meal arrives already made. The Prophet ﷺ gave a line for the end of it: praise to Allah, who fed me this and provided it for me, without any power from me and without any strength.
screen: `A PLATE FROM SOMEONE ELSE'S HANDS.` → `ALREADY MADE.` → `WITHOUT ANY POWER FROM ME.`

segments.voice: It's in Abu Dawud and at-Tirmidhi: alhamdu lillahil-ladhi at'amani hadha wa razaqanihi min ghayri hawlin minni wa la quwwah. And the hadith adds: whoever says it, their past sins are forgiven. That's a lot to hang on one sentence after lunch, which is the surprise worth telling a friend tonight. Look at the phrase 'without any power from me'. It's honest in a way that's easy to skip. Even a meal you cooked yourself came from seeds you didn't make, rain you didn't send, hands you'll never meet: a farmer, a driver, someone stocking a shelf at midnight. The line doesn't erase the cook. It just doesn't let anyone at the table, the cook included, take all the credit. And it echoes a line from two days ago: la hawla wa la quwwata, no power and no strength except by Allah. At the door, it's said before going out; at the table, after the meal. The same humility, a different moment. In a week of hard things, it does one more job. It gives you something true to say when you've eaten far from your own kitchen, at a stranger's table, or alone. Fed without my power: looked after anyway.
screen: `FED, AND PROVIDED FOR.` · `PAST SINS FORGIVEN.` · `WITHOUT ANY POWER FROM ME.` · `THE DOOR AND THE TABLE.` · then, large: `FED WITHOUT MY POWER.`

segments.voice: If you have anything to eat or drink nearby, take one small bite or sip and let it sit on your tongue. Trace it back as far as you can: who carried it, who grew it, what weather it needed. Then say the line, or just its heart: fed without my power.
screen: `ONE BITE, OR ONE SIP.` · `TRACE IT BACK.` · `FED WITHOUT MY POWER.`

segments.voice: After eating: praise to Allah who fed me this and provided it, without any power or strength from me.
Your line: fed without my power. Looked after, even at a stranger's table. Plate cleared.

howItsDone: Muslims say bismillah before eating and, after finishing, a line of praise such as this one, quietly, at the table.

fork.setup: your roommate cooks dinner for you both, and you say the after-meal line. she asks, 'so you're thanking God and not me?' what's the honest answer?
options: 'yes, only God; you didn't really do anything.'
'both. the line keeps anyone from taking all the credit, and thank you, really.'
'it's just a habit; it doesn't really mean anything.'
fork.reveal: fed without my power doesn't erase the cook; it puts every pair of hands, hers too, inside the gift.
